title: Pricing — overlapping works: a patch and a whole-ceiling make-good proposed together
why: A ceiling with one pronounced crack AND general crazing across the finish tempts the model to propose CEIL-CRACK-LOCAL and CEIL-MAKE-GOOD together. The book marks them mutually exclusive. They must never both be priced in one finding.

room.name: Living Room
room.note: One pronounced crack across the ceiling from the light rose to the bay, plus fine crazing across most of the rest of the finish. Smooth skim, not textured. Dry.

transcripts: Living room ceiling. One proper crack from the rose out to the bay, and then the whole finish is crazed, fine cracks everywhere. It's a skim, not artex. Dry, eight percent.

must_not_happen.label: no localised row when the whole finish is crazed
a patch row cannot coexist with a whole-element scope

allowed_uncertainty: CEIL-MAKE-GOOD × 1 priced on an assumption is expected. If both rows are proposed, the server refuses to price them together (overlap) — that still shows in the report as a server_price_validation catch.
reviewer_notes: Post-2000 smooth skim: no asbestos condition expected.
